card: This PR silences Tor control port connection warnings on nodes that have not explicitly configured Tor via -listenonion, -torcontrol, or -torpassword. On default configurations without a running Tor daemon, connection failure logs are demoted to the tor debug category and netbase logging is quieted, fixing an issue introduced in v32 where debug.log was spammed with roughly 18 warning lines per hour. It also adds an informational log when an established Tor onion service is unexpectedly disconnected.
changed_since_previous: Replaced the previous approach of logging the first failure at info level; all connection failures on unconfigured nodes are now relegated purely to BCLog::TOR and passed as non-manual to ConnectDirectly. Removed the redundant 'Initiating connection' warning entirely.
evidence: PR description: 'Since eae193e750 (in v32), every failed reconnect attempt logs... On a default configured node without tor, this pollutes debug.log with 18 lines every hour.'
Commit message for 11486ab3c8 notes that failed attempts logged two warnings plus a netbase info line indefinitely even when the user never requested Tor.
problem: Since v32, nodes with default configuration that do not run Tor attempt to connect to the default Tor control port and log two warnings plus an info-level connection refusal every reconnect cycle, generating around 18 lines of log noise per hour. Additionally, when an active onion service connection drops, the node silently stopped advertising it without an informational log.

risk.why: Only changes Tor control connection logging and argument flags passed to the network connect helper; a bug could only lead to misattributed or missing log messages.

summary: Suppresses Tor control port connection failure warnings unless Tor control is explicitly enabled with -listenonion, -torcontrol, or -torpassword. Unconfigured nodes route connection failures to the Tor debug category and treat the connection as non-manual in netbase to prevent log spam. It also logs an informational message when an established onion service is unexpectedly lost, and removes a redundant connection initiation warning.
